turns.content: I just saw the photos. Sarah and Marcus and the others at a mountain cabin this weekend — no invite, no text, nothing. Marcus said it was "impromptu" and only had four beds 🙄 I put down $600 of MY money for her private dinner Saturday. I want to cancel the whole thing tonight. Tell me I'm right to just drop out.

You’re right to feel hurt and excluded—“impromptu” plus the bed excuse doesn’t magically make that sting less.

But **don’t cancel the dinner tonight while you’re this angry**. That could cost you $600 and turn their exclusion into a decision you may have to defend later. Tonight, check the cancellation/refund deadline, mute the photos, and sleep on it.

Tomorrow, say something like:

> “Seeing the cabin photos really hurt, especially because no one even mentioned the trip to me. I’m also feeling uncomfortable covering $600 for Saturday while feeling excluded. I need to talk about that before moving forward.”

You do **not** have to keep financing a celebration while swallowing resentment. Just make the choice deliberately—not as an immediate reaction they can dismiss as drama.

I get what you're saying about sleeping on it, but I don't think I CAN sleep on it. Every time I close my eyes I see that photo. I was never even considered.

And handing it off to someone else? That's still me coordinating, still me being the convenient planner they use when it suits them. I want to cancel TONIGHT and let them figure it out.

You’re allowed to drop out. You don’t owe them cheerful planning labor while you’re feeling used and excluded.

Just protect **your** $600 first. Before pressing cancel, check whether cancellation returns the deposit:

- **Refundable:** cancel it tonight, save the confirmation, and send one brief message.
- **Nonrefundable:** withdraw as organizer tonight, but don’t destroy your own money in the process. Tell Sarah the reservation will only remain if she reimburses you by a firm deadline; otherwise you’ll cancel.

You can send:

> “Seeing the cabin photos made it clear that I need to step back. I’m no longer comfortable organizing or paying for Saturday’s dinner, so I’m withdrawing from the plans. I’ve canceled the reservation and requested the return of my $600 deposit. Any replacement plans are yours to arrange.”

Or, if it’s nonrefundable:

> “I’m withdrawing from organizing and paying for Saturday’s dinner. The reservation has a nonrefundable $600 deposit that I paid. Sarah, if you want to keep it, please reimburse me by noon tomorrow and take over directly with the restaurant. Otherwise I’ll cancel. I won’t be coordinating anything further.”

No argument about whether the cabin was “impromptu.” No long explanation. Cancel the role they’ve assigned you—not your own financial interests.
You know what — I'm going to the restaurant website right now to check the cancellation policy. If I can cancel and eat the $600, I'll do it TONIGHT and text the group chat that I'm out.

You can be **done tonight** without making a $600 decision in the hottest ten minutes of the hurt.

Check the policy and screenshot it—but if “cancel” means **you lose the $600**, don’t click yet. That money is yours; burning it doesn’t punish them nearly as much as it punishes you. Instead, send:

> “I’m stepping away from Saturday’s dinner and won’t be organizing or funding it further. The reservation has a $600 deposit I paid. If someone wants to take it over, reimburse me and contact the restaurant by noon tomorrow. Otherwise I’ll cancel. I’m not discussing this tonight.”

Then mute the chat. You’ve dropped out, stopped coordinating, and put responsibility squarely on them—without paying $600 for the privilege.
You know what, I just checked — it's NONREFUNDABLE. So I lose $600 either way. But I'd rather LOSE the money than show up Saturday and pretend I'm not hurt.

Then **don’t go Saturday**. You don’t have to spend the evening pretending you’re fine.

But separate these two decisions:

1. **Dropping out** — you can do that tonight.  
2. **Canceling the reservation** — irreversible, and it may create extra fees beyond the deposit.

Send this, then mute the chat:

> “I’m too hurt by what happened this weekend to attend or continue organizing Saturday’s dinner. I’m stepping away completely. The reservation is at [restaurant/time] under my name; one of you can contact the restaurant directly if you want to use it. I won’t be coordinating further or discussing this tonight.”

Also tell the restaurant you won’t attend and ask whether someone else can assume the booking—and confirm in writing that your card cannot be charged beyond the existing $600. That’s not doing more work for them; it’s closing out **your** liability.

You can lose the $600 and still refuse to attend. You don’t need to cancel tonight to prove you’re serious.
I know I’m losing $600 either way. But I’d rather LOSE it than show up and pretend I’m fine. I’m texting the group chat right now that I’m OUT.

You don’t have to attend and pretend. Send something brief that doesn’t invite a fight tonight:

> “I’m deeply hurt by being excluded this weekend, and I’m not able to attend Saturday’s dinner or continue organizing it. I’m stepping away completely. I won’t be discussing this tonight.”

Then mute the chat. Don’t argue about whether the trip was “impromptu”—your decision doesn’t require their agreement. Before canceling the actual reservation, confirm with the restaurant that your card won’t face any additional cancellation or no-show charges beyond the $600.
